subject: physics

sections.title: Introduction to Heat and Heat Transfer Methods
learning_objectives: Define heat as transfer of energy.

sections.title: Heat
learning_objectives: Define heat as transfer of energy.

sections.title: Temperature Change and Heat Capacity
learning_objectives: Observe heat transfer and change in temperature and mass.
Calculate final temperature after heat transfer between two objects.

sections.title: Phase Change and Latent Heat
learning_objectives: Examine heat transfer.
Calculate final temperature from heat transfer.

sections.title: Heat Transfer Methods
learning_objectives: Discuss the different methods of heat transfer.

sections.title: Conduction
learning_objectives: Calculate thermal conductivity.
Observe conduction of heat in collisions.
Study thermal conductivities of common substances.

sections.title: Convection
learning_objectives: Discuss the method of heat transfer by convection.

sections.title: Radiation
learning_objectives: Discuss heat transfer by radiation.
Explain the power of different materials.

sections.title: Introduction to Thermodynamics
learning_objectives: Define the first law of thermodynamics.

sections.title: The First Law of Thermodynamics
learning_objectives: Define the first law of thermodynamics.
Describe how conservation of energy relates to the first law of thermodynamics.
Identify instances of the first law of thermodynamics working in everyday situations, including biological metabolism.
Calculate changes in the internal energy of a system, after accounting for heat transfer and work done.

sections.title: The First Law of Thermodynamics and Some Simple Processes
learning_objectives: Describe the processes of a simple heat engine.
Explain the differences among the simple thermodynamic processes—isobaric, isochoric, isothermal, and adiabatic.
Calculate total work done in a cyclical thermodynamic process.

sections.title: Introduction to the Second Law of Thermodynamics: Heat Engines and Their Efficiency
learning_objectives: State the expressions of the second law of thermodynamics.
Calculate the efficiency and carbon dioxide emission of a coal-fired electricity plant, using second law characteristics.
Describe and define the Otto cycle.

sections.title: Carnot’s Perfect Heat Engine: The Second Law of Thermodynamics Restated
learning_objectives: Identify a Carnot cycle.
Calculate maximum theoretical efficiency of a nuclear reactor.
Explain how dissipative processes affect the ideal Carnot engine.

sections.title: Applications of Thermodynamics: Heat Pumps and Refrigerators
learning_objectives: Describe the use of heat engines in heat pumps and refrigerators.
Demonstrate how a heat pump works to warm an interior space.
Explain the differences between heat pumps and refrigerators.
Calculate a heat pump’s coefficient of performance.

sections.title: Entropy and the Second Law of Thermodynamics: Disorder and the Unavailability of Energy
learning_objectives: Define entropy and calculate the increase of entropy in a system with reversible and irreversible processes.
Explain the expected fate of the universe in entropic terms.
Calculate the increasing disorder of a system.

sections.title: Statistical Interpretation of Entropy and the Second Law of Thermodynamics: The Underlying Explanation
learning_objectives: Identify probabilities in entropy.
Analyze statistical probabilities in entropic systems.
